literal: Having examined and examined, he who does not accept friendship, in the end, to himself, dying grief will give.
translation: The friendship formed by one who does not repeatedly and thoroughly examine a person beforehand will, in the end, bring him grief that is fatal.
modern: மீண்டும் மீண்டும் ஆராய்ந்து பார்த்து ஒருவருடன் நட்புக்கொள்ளாதவனுடைய நட்பு, இறுதியில் அவனுக்குச் சாகுமளவிற்குத் துன்பத்தைத் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the critical importance of thoroughly testing a person's character before befriending them. The repetition of the word 'ayntu' (having examined) highlights that scrutiny must be continuous and rigorous, not a casual or one-time affair. If one enters into a friendship blindly without such careful investigation, that relationship will eventually bring immense, life-threatening sorrow. The word 'kaṭaimuṟai' indicates the ultimate, inevitable outcome of such carelessness, while 'cām tuyaram' vividly describes a grief so intense that it feels like death itself.
